paper.title_en: Macroscopic properties of fermionic dark matter mixed neutron stars
paper.abstract_en: This study systematically investigates the macroscopic properties of fermionic dark matter mixed neutron stars, where baryonic matter and dark matter are coupled solely through gravitational interactions. The baryonic equation of state is constructed within the relativistic mean-field framework and includes the full baryon octet. The equilibrium stellar structure is determined by solving the coupled two-fluid TOV equations. To characterize the uncertainty in the dark matter distribution, we introduced three central boundary conditions with clear physical significance: a fixed dark matter fraction (fm), a fixed central energy density ratio (fε), and a fixed central pressure ratio (fp). Results indicate a systematic and consistent trend across all three boundary conditions: as these three parameters increase, the maximum stable mass decreases, while the gravitational wave frequency and amplitude at the end of the binary inspiral phase increase monotonically. Compared with DM core-dominated configurations, the presence of a DM halo leads to more complex behaviors of the f-mode frequency and tidal deformability. At fixed central energy density ratio fε, increasing the DM self-interaction strength Cvd can cause the maximum mass of DM halo mixed stars to exceed that of purely hadronic neutron stars. These results demonstrate that the macroscopic properties of dark matter mixed stars are highly sensitive to the equation of state, the two-fluid treatment, and the choice of boundary conditions. They provide systematic theoretical predictions for constraining DM properties through joint measurements of tidal deformabilities, stellar oscillation frequencies, and inspiral waveforms with next-generation gravitational wave detectors.
